thread:
Alex: FYI I'm seeing a pattern where pages go into a 'dormant' state and then we spike evictions during long-context runs when KV is stored in INT8. Repro attached below. Could use eyes on whether this is an eviction heuristic bug or quantization-induced noise. :thinking:

Shayla: Can you paste the repro steps and the config? Is this on private or hosted infra?

Alex: Private cluster (g5dn replica). Quick steps: run long-context sweep (ctx=64k) with model_xx-int8-kv enabled, workload = many short queries + occasional 16k prompts. Config snippet:
```
kv.cache.enabled = true
kv.eviction.policy = "adaptive"
kv.eviction.dormancy_ttl_ms = 120000
kv.page_size_kb = 256
quant.level = "int8"
batcher.max_tokens = 4096
```
Profiler snapshot shows repeated page flip sequences where a page marked dormant is reactivated immediately and another page gets evicted.

Michael: Interesting. Two quick hypotheses: 1) our dormancy TTL is too short for the long-tail access pattern, so pages thrash between hot and dormant states. 2) INT8 aliasing reduces the effective uniqueness of keys so reuse detection misfires and we treat warmed pages as cold.

Priya: I ran a small experiment to vary dormancy_ttl and page_size. Summary (30-min runs):
- TTL=30s, page=128KB: mem_peak=21.8GB, evictions=12.3k, quality_delta=+1.4% perplexity (worse)
- TTL=120s, page=256KB: mem_peak=14.7GB, evictions=1.6k, quality_delta=+0.9%
- TTL=300s, page=512KB: mem_peak=13.9GB, evictions=400, quality_delta=+1.1%
Memory savings vs FP16 baseline: INT8 reduced KV footprint ~44% in all runs, but the short TTL case had huge eviction churn which correlated with worst quality regressions.

Alex: Nice. So INT8 buys memory, but if we evict too eagerly we lose cached prefixes and blow up compute in ways that harm output quality. Do we have traces tying specific evictions to cache-misses on high-attention tokens?

Priya: I instrumented reuse_score per page. When reuse_score < 0.2 we treat as dormant. In INT8 runs we saw more pages hover at ~0.18-0.25 boundary vs BF16 where they stayed >0.4. Seems quantization compresses difference between frequently- and infrequently-used KV vectors.

Michael: That suggests we should either: 1) increase dormancy threshold when quantized, or 2) use a hybrid metric that incorporates last-access recency + reuse_score delta after dequantization, or 3) prefer page-granularity compaction instead of immediate eviction. I vote for (2) plus a short hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.

Shayla: Will that interact badly with batching heuristics? If pages stick around longer we'll need to ensure we don't regress latency SLOs on memory-limited nodes. Also, kernel selection: smaller pages help kernel memory utilization but increase metadata overhead.

Priya: I did a follow-up with a hysteresis + quant-aware threshold: set reuse_threshold = base*0.65 when quantized and add a 2-touch hysteresis window (must be cold for 2 consecutive TTLs). Results: mem_peak=15.1GB, evictions=820, quality_delta=+0.2% (almost back to baseline). Throughput unchanged.

perf-bot: perf-run 1790012450: model_xx-int8 longctx suite completed. baseline_fp16=1000 tokens/s, int8_no_hyst=980 tokens/s, int8_with_hyst=997 tokens/s. mem_peak delta int8_with_hyst vs fp16 = -41%

Alex: That's encouraging. Next actions: Priya, can you run longer (4h) with the hysteresis config and capture per-page reuse histograms and full eval set to check for small quality regressions across prompts? Michael/Shayla, can you review kernel-level interactions (page size vs cuBLAS/use of fused attention kernels) to ensure no hidden latency cliff?

Michael: On it. I'll also check if different kernel variants (small-page vs large-page codepath) affect the effective reuse_score because of runtime scheduling.

Shayla: I'll model the SLO impact with memory pressure sim and ensure autoscaler interacts well with the change. Will flag if we need to adjust batcher.max_tokens to protect latency.

Priya: Starting the 4h run now with logging at 1-min granularity. Will post histograms + eval numbers when done. :thumbsup:

Alex: Thanks team. If this looks good after the 4h run we should land a conservative opt-in and then A/B on a small shard. Also add a diagnostic that logs when a quantized page is evicted with reuse_score between 0.15 and 0.3 so we can trace later.
